issues.description: Class 'Bitmap24' in the template header declares its data members, constructors, destructor and all member functions under a private: section (making them inaccessible). The template's main.cpp constructs a Bitmap24 instance and calls resize_buffer() and set() (calls at example_program/src/main.cpp), so those members must be public for the example to compile. The solution's Bitmap24.hpp exposes these members as public. This visibility mismatch will cause the provided example to fail to compile and will block students from running the example program.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Bitmap24 API in the template header public to match its usage and the solution. Add a public: access specifier (or move the constructors, destructor and methods such as resize_buffer, save and set into a public: section) so main.cpp can construct Bitmap24 and call its methods. This preserves the pedagogical content while ensuring the example and tests compile.
